env.#3: Unset here on purpose: config/packages/storage.yaml selects the LOCAL adapter,
env.#4: which needs none of these, and a half-filled S3 block is how a deployment ends
env.#5: up failing on its first upload rather than at compile time. To move the bytes

contents: # Evidence storage (uhifadhi/storage-module) — where field photographs live.
# There is deliberately no flysystem.yaml beside this file: the storage bundle
# PREPENDS its own `storage.evidence` storage, private on both visibility axes,
# and a hand-written one would only be a second, weaker definition of it.
# Everything below is the bundle's own default, written out so it can be read
# and changed. Delete the whole `storage:` key and nothing breaks — a fresh
# installation already has a working, private, on-disk evidence store.
# Outside the document root, as it must be: nothing here is reachable without
# passing the authenticated serving route, which asks the owning module whether
# this reader may see this photograph.
storage:
evidence:
adapter: local
directory: '%kernel.project_dir%/var/storage/evidence'
files:
# Seeing where every file is kept is seeing something about all of them
# at once — gate it with the module-configuration permission the core's
# team bundle publishes; without a permission catalogue, delete this
# line and the bundle falls back to ROLE_ADMIN.
# What YOU call the place files go. Unset, the hub says "This server" or
# "Object storage" according to the adapter, and never invents a vendor.
storage_label: 'This server'
storage_location: 'Local disk'
# AN INSTALLATION THAT ALREADY HAS PHOTOGRAPHS points `directory` at them
# instead of moving them. Keys are RELATIVE and are recorded on the owning
# module's rows, so a path that was already a valid key stays one — not a row is
# rewritten and not a photograph goes dark. The owning module's voter claims
# whatever prefix those keys carry, alongside the one new uploads use.
# PRODUCTION (any S3-compatible object storage) — the same bundle drives it with
# no code change. Switch by adding, in a deploy-time override:
#   composer require league/flysystem-async-aws-s3
#   storage:
#       evidence:
#           adapter: s3
#               endpoint: '%env(STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT)%'
#               bucket:   '%env(STORAGE_S3_BUCKET)%'
#               region:   '%env(STORAGE_S3_REGION)%'
#               key:      '%env(STORAGE_S3_KEY)%'
#               secret:   '%env(STORAGE_S3_SECRET)%'
#               path_style_endpoint: true   # where the provider addresses buckets as endpoint/bucket
# The bucket must be private at the bucket level too: the bundle marks every
# object private, but a public bucket policy overrides that from outside.
# Existing photographs are copied up first (`rclone`/`aws s3 sync` of the
# directory above, keys unchanged) — the keys are relative precisely so that
# move costs no database work.
# The ONE way stored evidence comes back out (uhifadhi/storage-module).
# Only the serving controller is mounted, by file rather than by directory: the
# bundle also carries a cross-module Files hub, and mounting that is a separate
# decision about a separate screen, not a side effect of wanting photographs to
# appear on an observation.
# The route itself only exists where SecurityBundle is in the kernel — the bundle
# registers no controller without it, so a deployment can never end up serving
# field photographs from an unauthenticated endpoint.
# The whole controller directory: serving AND the Files hub (/files — the
# cross-module registry the sidebar's "Files" entry opens).
storage:
resource: '@UhifadhiStorageBundle/src/Controller/'
type: attribute
